title: Everyone is building AI agents. Who's designing the stop button?
description: As AI agents gain autonomy to interpret and act independently, designers face a critical challenge: defining where human control ends and AI begins. This essay explores the hardest design decisions in AI products—not how to make agents smarter, but how to make them stoppable and transparent.

title: Building an AI-ready design system library
description: A practical guide on structuring design systems for the AI era, starting in code before syncing to Figma. This approach enables better maintainability, automation, and integration with AI-assisted design workflows, making it essential reading for teams modernizing their design infrastructure.

title: Agents struggle with the same bad UX we do
description: AI agents reveal our worst UX sins—they can't guess, improvise, or ask for help. This article argues that agents are our most honest usability testers, forcing designers to confront how poor interface design affects both humans and machine learning systems.

title: Pick three
description: A thought-provoking exploration of the design paradox: good, fast, and cheap are mutually exclusive. This essay unpacks the hidden costs of creative work and challenges the common misconception that quality is always negotiable.

title: I let AI build. I don't let AI decide.
description: A practical framework for deciding where to trust AI in your workflow versus where human judgment is non-negotiable. The author shares concrete examples of tasks they confidently delegate to models versus decisions they scrutinize, offering actionable guidance for product teams navigating AI integration.

title: Modern CSS Might Make Your Front-End More Complex
description: While modern CSS features can eliminate JavaScript dependencies, they risk fragmenting logic across the codebase and making applications harder to maintain. Gabriel Shoyombo examines the trade-offs between local optimizations and systemic complexity that designers and developers need to consider.

title: The window with no buttons
description: Why the terminal intimidates designers and how to demystify it. A practical guide to understanding command-line interfaces, helping designers build better mental models of how developers work and improving cross-functional collaboration.

title: How to hire junior engineers in the age of AI
description: Junior developer hiring has collapsed as AI commoditizes entry-level coding tasks. This article proposes new hiring frameworks for identifying talent when traditional skill assessments no longer differentiate candidates, raising important questions about how teams build and onboard in an AI-assisted world.
